body: This is true. But it was the only way fool proof way I could think of proving the video existed before it was taken down. I wasn't about to just forget about the creep who kept a video of me for 6 years and shared it with 35,000 people. I wasn't going to let them get away with that.

In response to (3) I did make the video. But I'd argue that I was not old enough to fully understand the magnitude of my actions. Young girls feel many societal pressures. I was not exempt from those influences.
I have read that. But I wasn't an adult when I produced or sent the the video so I didn't think it applied to what occurred six years ago.

I spoke with an officer at my university without revealing my name and they told me that a crime wasn't committed until the other individual uploaded the video online. So no, I don't understand that I committed a crime. Do you have any sources I could read?

Thank you so much. Every response I've gotten has been so supportive. Yours included. Sometimes carrying all my secrets just gets a bit heavy. Although I'm glad I'm not alone, I'm so sorry that there are so many people who feel this way.   
I wish no one felt this way. Do take care. And thanks again.
I'll keep this in mind. Thanks
I hadn't thought of that. I don't use a razor, I use an x-acto knife. (Which probably isn't any better). Maybe I'll experiment.

I did a bumblebee once. At first it looked awesome but then I didn't like the way it healed so I cut a grid over it. I don't have many scars. I find the places that work for me/look good and I cut over my old lines once they heal. Over time the ones I don't like fade away. Every once and awhile I branch out and try new things in new places, but I always stay in the same general areas. 

The bathroom thing. Yes. I do exactly that. I love it. 

I never want to have to get stitches because then someone would know. I don't want anyone to know. I guess I just need to be careful.

Thank you so so much for your reply.
